_comment: Pattern rules for the tool_coach PreToolUse hook (hooks/tool_coach.py).
Each rule: a regex matched against the Bash `command` string, after heredoc
bodies have been stripped. First match wins. On match the tool call is DENIED
and `message` is shown to the model as the redirect (a permissionDecisionReason).
The goal is to replace a dead-end 'permission denied' with a 'do THIS instead'
so the model stops retrying variants.
Deletions and out-of-project paths are NOT rules here: they are structural
checks in tool_coach.py, which parses the command's argv so it also catches
the wrapped, absolute-path and pipeline forms a regex would miss.
Order matters: put more-specific patterns above broader ones (the inline-snippet
rule must precede the bare-interpreter rule). Edit this file freely - no code
change needed. Patterns are Python `re` syntax.

rules.name: no-python-dash-c
rules.message: Blocked: an inline -c snippet. Ad-hoc inline code leaves no auditable trace of what ran. Instead, write a real script FILE under tmp/ (for example tmp/<descriptive_name>.py) and run it with `uv run tmp/<descriptive_name>.py`. Treat the script as a named artifact you can re-read, diff and re-run. This applies to every variant, including the ones wrapped in `uv run`.

rules.name: no-bare-python
rules.message: Blocked: a direct interpreter invocation. This environment standardizes on uv so the correct virtualenv is always active. Run a module with `uv run -m <pkg.module>`, a script with `uv run <script.py>`, or for a subproject `uv run --directory <subproject> ...`. Re-run through uv rather than calling the interpreter directly.

rules.name: no-pythonpath
rules.message: Blocked: setting the PYTHONPATH= environment variable. Let uv manage the import path instead of injecting it manually - use `uv run` (or `uv run --directory <subproject>`), which activates the right environment and resolves imports correctly.

rules.name: no-timeout-binary
rules.message: Blocked: the timeout(1) binary. Use the Bash tool's own timeout parameter (in milliseconds) to bound a command instead of wrapping it in the timeout executable.
